title: Fall back to a GitHub-hosted runner when no self-hosted runner is online
excerpt: On 2026-11-04 an audit of the <org> workflows (Coder, IronClaude, IronOrca) set out to move every job to the org's self-hosted runners. Each job would fall back to a GitHub-hosted runner only when no matching self-hosted runner is online. The owner kept the move to self-hosted and parked the fallback here. Findings so far: - **No built-in fallback.** GitHub Actions has no fallback runner; `runs-on` labels only queue a job until a matching runner picks it up. - **The candidate pattern.** A small first job on a hosted runner asks the REST API for an online self-hosted runner with the needed labels. It outputs a `runs-on` value, and later jobs use `runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.<job>.outputs.<x>) }}`. Define it once, as a reusable workflow or composite action. - **Costs of that pattern.*
